findings.issue_text: [High/security] In UsersResource.java:448, the per-user `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` was removed from `searchForUser` and the `UserModel.GROUPS` restriction is only applied when `groupIds` is non-empty, so an admin with only the `query-users` role (no global view permission and no group view-members grants) now receives the full unrestricted user list instead of an empty filtered result; the PR's own test `testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers` expects an initially empty search, so either the code or the test is wrong, and the code as shown discloses all realm users.

[High/security] In GroupPermissionsV2.java:~68, `canManage()` evaluates `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`, accepting the `view` scope for a manage check, so an admin granted only 'view' on the Groups resource type passes `requireManage()` and can create groups via `GroupsResource.addGroup`; this contradicts `canManage(GroupModel)` which correctly checks only MANAGE, and the javadoc added to `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage` codifies the same copy-paste error.

[Medium/bug] In GroupPermissionsV2.java:~104, `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` only collects groups with explicit per-group resources while `canViewMembers()` additionally grants groups without resources via the all-groups fallback in `hasPermission()`, so for admins holding a type-level (all-groups) VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grant the search restriction diverges from actual permissions — unrestricted/over-inclusive (e.g., users in no group) when no group resources exist, or hiding members of viewable groups when some do; search results and `canView(user)` disagree.

[Medium/bug] In UserPermissions.java:585 and GroupPermissions.java:323, dropping `root.users().canManage()` from `canViewByGroup` (and from `requireViewMembers` via `canViewMembers`) breaks existing V1 FGAP admins granted only the 'manage' permission on the Users resource: they can still manage users (`canManageByGroup` → `canManageMembers` still honors `canManage`) but now get 403 when viewing them — a manage-without-view inconsistency and a silent behavior regression for existing deployments.

[Medium/api] In GroupPermissionsV2.java:~162, the `GroupPermissionManagement` overrides (`setPermissionsEnabled`, `managePermission`, `resource`, `getPermissions`, etc.) throw raw `UnsupportedOperationException`, but existing infrastructure still invokes them — notably the `GroupRemovedEvent` handler in `AdminPermissions.registerListener` (AdminPermissions.java:~94) calls `groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false)` during every group deletion when the feature is enabled, so group deletion will throw/500 if `management()` resolves to the V2 evaluator for V2 realms; these should no-op or callers must be guarded.

[Medium/performance] In GroupResource.java:177 and GroupsResource.java:112, removing the `canViewGlobal` short-circuit means every group now goes through `canView(g)`, which in V2 is a `findByName` resource lookup plus a full policy evaluation per group with no global check first, degrading group listing to O(n) authorization evaluations per request for permission-based admins in large realms.

[Medium/test_gap] GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java has no negative coverage for the scenarios the implementation gets wrong: a `query-users`-only admin searching users (the new test's initial `assertTrue(search.isEmpty())` would fail against this code), a view-only all-groups permission attempting group creation (would catch the canManage issue), and all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS search consistency.
[Low/doc_defect] In GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:~145, the `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` javadoc says '@return Stream of IDs of groups' but the method actually returns `Set<String>`.

[Low/doc_defect] In GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:~137, the `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` javadoc references `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` instead of `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`, making the enforced check ambiguous.

goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/security] In UsersResource.java:448, the per-user `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` was removed from `searchForUser` and the `UserModel.GROUPS` restriction is only applied when `groupIds` is non-empty, so an admin with only the `query-users` role (no global view permission and no group view-members grants) now receives the full unrestricted user list instead of an empty filtered result; the PR's own test `testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers` expects an initially empty search, so either the code or the test is wrong, and the code as shown discloses all realm users.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser(...)` the diff removes the explicit per-user authorization gate: `session.users().searchForUserStream(...).filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` is replaced with an unfiltered stream passed into `toRepresentation(...)`. At the same time, the only remaining restriction mechanism in this method is setting `session` attribute `UserModel.GROUPS` *only when* `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is non-empty. For an admin who can query users but has neither global view/manage users nor any group `view-members/manage-members` grants, `groupIds` will be empty, the session attribute is not set, and the search stream is no longer filtered—so the method can return users the caller cannot view. This directly contradicts the test expectation added/used in `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers`, which expects the initial search to be empty before granting `VIEW_MEMBERS`.

This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

The candidate flags that GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() incorrectly calls hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), allowing VIEW-only admins to pass a manage/write check. This is the same underlying bug described in the golden comment (canManage should require MANAGE only, while canView can accept VIEW or MANAGE).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] In GroupPermissionsV2.java:~104, `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` only collects groups with explicit per-group resources while `canViewMembers()` additionally grants groups without resources via the all-groups fallback in `hasPermission()`, so for admins holding a type-level (all-groups) VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grant the search restriction diverges from actual permissions — unrestricted/over-inclusive (e.g., users in no group) when no group resources exist, or hiding members of viewable groups when some do; search results and `canView(user)` disagree.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` builds the restriction set by iterating authorization **resources** (`resourceStore.findByType(...)`) and adding `groupResource.getId()` (authorization resource id), while permission checks elsewhere (eg `canViewMembers(GroupModel group)`) operate on the **group id** (`group.getId()`) and `hasPermission()` looks up resources by **name** via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. This mismatch means the set used for user-search restriction can diverge from actual `canViewMembers()`/`canView(user)` evaluation, especially with type-level (all-groups) permissions and/or when not all groups have per-group resources, leading to inconsistent/hiding/incorrect search results.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] In UserPermissions.java:585 and GroupPermissions.java:323, dropping `root.users().canManage()` from `canViewByGroup` (and from `requireViewMembers` via `canViewMembers`) breaks existing V1 FGAP admins granted only the 'manage' permission on the Users resource: they can still manage users (`canManageByGroup` → `canManageMembers` still honors `canManage`) but now get 403 when viewing them — a manage-without-view inconsistency and a silent behavior regression for existing deployments.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the V1 shortcut that treated user-manage capability as sufficient for viewing users via group membership. Previously, `UserPermissions.canViewByGroup` evaluated `root.groups().getGroupsWithViewPermission(group)`, and `GroupPermissions.getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel)` returned `true` when `root.users().canView() || root.users().canManage()`. This meant an admin who could manage users (e.g., via Users-resource MANAGE scope) would also pass the group-based view path. Now `canViewByGroup` uses `root.groups()::canViewMembers` and `GroupPermissions.requireViewMembers` uses `canViewMembers(group)`, which only short-circuits on `root.users().canView()` (not `canManage()`) and otherwise requires group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS scopes. So a manage-only Users permission can still enable managing users (via `canManageByGroup` -> `canManageMembers`, which still short-circuits on `root.users().canManage()`), but may no longer enable viewing them, creating the regression/inconsistency described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] In GroupPermissionsV2.java:~162, the `GroupPermissionManagement` overrides (`setPermissionsEnabled`, `managePermission`, `resource`, `getPermissions`, etc.) throw raw `UnsupportedOperationException`, but existing infrastructure still invokes them — notably the `GroupRemovedEvent` handler in `AdminPermissions.registerListener` (AdminPermissions.java:~94) calls `groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false)` during every group deletion when the feature is enabled, so group deletion will throw/500 if `management()` resolves to the V2 evaluator for V2 realms; these should no-op or callers must be guarded.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AdminPermissions.registerListener` (still under `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ`) handling `GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent` by calling `management(session, realm).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getGroup(), false)`. The diff also shows `MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()` now returns `new GroupPermissionsV2(...)`, and in `GroupPermissionsV2` the `GroupPermissionManagement` methods including `setPermissionsEnabled(...)` are overridden to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. If a realm uses `MgmtPermissionsV2` for management(), then group deletion will trigger this listener path and throw at runtime, causing a 500 during deletion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] In GroupResource.java:177 and GroupsResource.java:112, removing the `canViewGlobal` short-circuit means every group now goes through `canView(g)`, which in V2 is a `findByName` resource lookup plus a full policy evaluation per group with no global check first, degrading group listing to O(n) authorization evaluations per request for permission-based admins in large realms.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the `canViewGlobal` pre-check in both `GroupResource#getSubGroups` and `GroupsResource#getGroups`, changing filters from `canViewGlobal || canView(g)` to always calling `canView(g)` per group (`.filter(auth.groups()::canView)` / `.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView)`). In V2, `GroupPermissionsV2#canView(GroupModel)` calls `hasPermission(group.getId(), ...)`, which performs a per-group `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` and then a permission evaluation (and may still fall back to the resource-type “all-groups” evaluation). Previously, a single `groupsEvaluator.canView()` could short-circuit per-group checks when the caller had global group-view permission. This is a diff-grounded potential performance regression for large group listings, but not a functional defect per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java has no negative coverage for the scenarios the implementation gets wrong: a `query-users`-only admin searching users (the new test's initial `assertTrue(search.isEmpty())` would fail against this code), a view-only all-groups permission attempting group creation (would catch the canManage issue), and all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS search consistency.

adjudication.rationale: The finding is about missing negative test coverage for newly added/changed permission logic. The diff introduces nontrivial behavior changes (e.g., `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`, so a VIEW-only “all-groups” permission could incorrectly satisfy manage checks, but `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest` never asserts that VIEW-only cannot create groups). Also, the test setup now grants `myadmin` both `QUERY_USERS` and `QUERY_GROUPS` (RealmAdminPermissionsConfig), so it does not exercise a `query-users`-only admin case. Additionally, `UsersResource.searchForUser` removed the `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` and now relies on `session` attributes (`UserModel.GROUPS`) for restriction, which is a behavior worth negative-testing but isn’t covered by the new tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] In GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:~145, the `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` javadoc says '@return Stream of IDs of groups' but the method actually returns `Set<String>`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a Javadoc mismatch in GroupPermissionEvaluator: the comment for getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() says “@return Stream of IDs...” while the method signature returns Set<String>. However, this is purely a documentation/style defect and does not represent broken behavior introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] In GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:~137, the `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` javadoc references `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` instead of `canManageMembers(GroupModel)`, making the enforced check ambiguous.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionEvaluator` the Javadoc above `requireManageMembers(GroupModel group)` says: "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns {@code false}." However, the method name suggests it should reference `canManageMembers(GroupModel)` (which exists just above) rather than `canManageMembership(GroupModel)`. This is a documentation mismatch introduced/visible in the diff, not a functional defect.
